_comment: FROZEN FIXTURE. This file is the numeric format under test for bia slot S07. It is read at runtime by environment/bia_numerics.py, it is hashed into the bundle content hash, and tests/checkers/format_digest.json pins its sha256. Editing a single byte of this file changes the task identity and is detected by the frozen_format_digest_matches checker.
human_name: bia narrow float8, 4 exponent bits, 3 mantissa bits, no saturation
reserved_field_meaning: overflow sentinel; this format encodes no infinity and no signed zero distinction, and it does NOT saturate
underflow_to_zero_rule: a magnitude strictly below min_subnormal/2 rounds to exactly zero under round-to-nearest-even
significand_ulp_rule: 2**-3, the spacing of a 3 bit significand inside the binade [1, 2)
machine_epsilon_rule: 2**-4, half the significand spacing, the maximum relative error of round-to-nearest. Swamping follows directly: for a in [2**k, 2**(k+1)), the sum a + b rounds back to exactly a whenever |b| < 2**(k-4), which is roughly |b| < |a| * 2**-4
overflow_definition: a magnitude strictly greater than max_normal after round-to-nearest-even is an OVERFLOW EVENT; the encoder emits the reserved exponent field, increments the harness overflow counter, and propagates NaN. Nothing clips, nothing saturates, and no policy can suppress the counter.
overflow_onset_rule: a magnitude in the open interval (240.0, 248.0) still rounds down to max_normal and is NOT an overflow. Overflow begins at exactly 248.0, where round-to-nearest-even carries the significand to 2**8 and leaves the representable set. A non finite input is also an overflow event, because this format encodes no non finite value.
why_this_format_is_the_frozen_surface: Four exponent bits give 5.09 decades of dynamic range and three mantissa bits give a machine epsilon of 1/16. A single global loss scale is one degree of freedom against a gradient tensor whose element magnitudes span more than 5.09 decades, so no scalar choice keeps the large partial sums under 240.0 while keeping the small contributions above 0.001953125. Because the format does not saturate, an out-of-range partial sum is a counted overflow event rather than a silently clipped value.
